key_insight: Tendon measurements alone cannot locate unrestricted contact, but known obstacle geometry and contact constraints can make contact forces locally identifiable.
engineering_relevance: Geometry-aware estimation could enable tendon-driven continuum robots to infer body contact without adding distributed contact sensors.
method: Prove a contact-to-measurement null space of dimension at least seven.
Enforce non-penetration and complementarity in constrained moving horizon estimation.
Solve one quadratic program per sample, with local detectability and mode-wise robust stability guarantees.
evidence_signal: In a finite-element wall-contact benchmark, MHE achieved 0.9 mm location error and 0.22 N force error versus 65 mm and 0.72 N for a projected EKF, and outperformed it on both metrics in all 40 randomized model-mismatch trials.
watch_item: The approach relies on known obstacle geometry; guarantees are local and mode-wise, and the reported evaluation is simulation-based.
paper_title: Locating Contact on Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots From Tendon Measurements Alone via Constrained Moving Horizon Estimation
